statements.quote: A preregistered 2×2 factorial randomized controlled trial conducted at a leading European university provides data from 1,053 first-year undergraduate students enrolled in 13 classes of the same first basic management course of three bachelor programs in economics & management (E&M), economics & finance (E&F), and management (M).
statements.locator: PDF p. 2 [printed p. 1], Section 1, Introduction, paragraph beginning with the preregistered trial.

statements.quote: Figure 1 shows the experiment flow; Sections 1 through 4 of the Appendix provide the full design, rubrics, and measures. Section 5 in the Appendix provides balance checks.
statements.locator: PDF p. 3 [printed p. 2], Section 1, Introduction, paragraph above Figure 1.

statements.quote: To preserve authors’ anonymity, we do not disclose the name of the university and the registration number of the pre-analysis plan with the American Economic Association’s registry for randomized controlled trials.
statements.locator: PDF p. 3 [printed p. 2], Footnote 2.

statements.quote: Section 3 of the Appendix describes the details of the rubric and the text evaluations.
statements.locator: PDF p. 6 [printed p. 5], Section 3, Causal reasoning, final paragraph before Section 4.

statements.quote: Section 2 of the Appendix explains the performance measure, provides details about the rubric and the training of the evaluators and reports statistics about inter-rater reliability.
statements.locator: PDF p. 8 [printed p. 7], Section 4.2, Performance: Awareness and Usage, opening paragraph on this page.

statements.quote: Section 4 in the Appendix describes the construction of these three variables.
statements.locator: PDF p. 10 [printed p. 9], Section 4.3, Ideas: Number and Diversity.

statements.quote: This document contains the following additional material: • Section 1: Experimental design and flow • Section 2: Performance evaluation: rubric, evaluators’ training and inter-rater reliability • Section 3: Causal reasoning measurement • Section 4: Variables construction • Section 5: Descriptive statistics and balance table • Section 6: Tables with estimated results
statements.locator: PDF p. 17 [printed p. 16], Appendix, contents list.

statements.quote: The study was pre-registered with the AEA RCT Registry [link currently not available to preserve anonymity] prior to data collection and received ethics approval from the University’s Ethics Committee.
statements.locator: PDF p. 17 [printed p. 16], Appendix Section 1, Experimental design and flow, first paragraph.

statements.quote: Materials were administered in English for E&M and E&F and in the national language for M.
statements.locator: PDF p. 17 [printed p. 16], Appendix Section 1, Experimental design and flow, second paragraph.

statements.quote: Completion times were logged, with students allowed to finish earlier than the total allocated time, or to stay a few minutes longer if needed to complete the assignment.
statements.locator: PDF p. 17 [printed p. 16], Appendix Section 1, Experimental design and flow, session description.

statements.quote: The session closed with a post-treatment survey that repeated the baseline attitude items, recorded self-reported strategic approach and ChatGPT usage, and invited participants in the AI arms to share their conversation logs.
statements.locator: PDF p. 18 [printed p. 17], Appendix Section 1, Experimental design and flow, final survey description.

statements.quote: The recommendations were then assessed by a set of evaluators on the notion of awareness and usage from the marketing literature and were given a detailed rubric with the criteria based on these concepts (see Section 2 of this Appendix).
statements.locator: PDF p. 18 [printed p. 17], Appendix Section 1, Experimental design and flow, final paragraph.

statements.quote: Each pre-registered scale level is operationalized through explicit anchored descriptors and worked examples, with the rater training in §2.3 ensuring consistent application.
statements.locator: PDF p. 19 [printed p. 18], Appendix Section 2.1, Definition and Measurement.

statements.quote: Recruitment materials described the task in general terms, namely, as a structured rating exercise on business consulting.
statements.locator: PDF p. 22 [printed p. 21], Appendix Section 2.3, Evaluators’ Recruitment, first paragraph.

statements.quote: Throughout both the training and rating phases, evaluators had continuous access to the rating rubric, a written codebook elaborating each construct with examples, and a full video recording of the initial practice session for reference. These materials were made available to support consistent application of the rubric and to allow evaluators to resolve ambiguities by consulting the codebook rather than relying on memory or peer consultation during active rating.
statements.locator: PDF p. 22 [printed p. 21], Appendix Section 2.3, Evaluators’ Recruitment, paragraph on rubric, codebook and training video access.

statements.quote: Evaluators were not permitted to take stimulus materials off-site, nor to discuss specific stimuli or their ratings with one another outside of the structured calibration discussions.
statements.locator: PDF p. 22 [printed p. 21], Appendix Section 2.3, Evaluators’ Recruitment, on-site stimulus restrictions.

statements.quote: We retained complete sampling logs, including case identifiers, evaluator identifiers, assignment timestamps, and arm membership, for all 3,159 ratings (1,053 X 3).
statements.locator: PDF p. 23 [printed p. 22], Appendix Section 2.4, Performance Evaluations, first paragraph.

statements.quote: We use LLMs to transform qualitative observations into quantifiable scores via a 5-point Likert scale with the same pre-registered operationalized anchoring criteria for the three distinct attributes.
statements.locator: PDF p. 25 [printed p. 24], Appendix Section 3.1, Measurement, preregistered scoring anchors.

statements.quote: Prompts: System prompt contains the full case text (Bocconi merchandising scenario), rubric definitions with scoring anchors (1–5 for each dimension), bilingual instructions (English/Italian), mandatory chain-of-thought extraction step before scoring, and output format specification. User prompt contains only the student response text.
statements.locator: PDF p. 29 [printed p. 28], Appendix Section 3.3, LLM-based Causal Reasoning Evaluations, Technical details.

statements.quote: The full system and user prompts for the causal-reasoning evaluation are reproduced below verbatim; the {{response}} placeholder in the user prompt is replaced at runtime by each student’s response text.
statements.locator: PDF p. 29 [printed p. 28], Appendix Section 3.3, LLM-based Causal Reasoning Evaluations; the prompts themselves occupy PDF pp. 29-36 [printed pp. 28-35].

statements.quote: Text based measures were computed from the raw case response text using measures adapted from Kusumegi et al. (2025), implemented in compute_text_complexity.py. These measures serve as HD variables in the PDS Lasso estimations.
statements.locator: PDF p. 38 [printed p. 37], Appendix Section 4, Variables construction, Text-based variables.

notes:
Checked on 2026-10-10 UTC (2026-10-09 in America/New_York). Read the entire 129,195-character markdown conversion, including all six Appendix sections and the final references, and verified relevant quotations by extracting the corresponding pages from the 49-page PDF. Quotations retain the source wording, with PDF line wrapping and line-break hyphenation normalized. The PDF contains no hyperlink annotations and no embedded files. The source is the saved August 2026 OpenAI-hosted report associated with CEPR DP 21882; the CEPR version could not be compared.

No data-availability statement, public data/code repository URL, or offer to provide data on request was found. The form data_and_code.data_url and code_url are both empty. The AEA registration number and link are expressly withheld for anonymity. compute_text_complexity.py is named but no location or access conditions are supplied. Retained rating logs and conversation-log collection describe internal data handling, not public availability. Rubrics, the business case, scoring prompts, variable definitions and aggregate tables appear inside the paper; these in-document materials are not counted as a separate data/code deposit. Therefore deposits is empty and status is none_found, rather than restricted or on_request.

The existing report URL https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/novices-and-llm-august-2026.pdf returned HTTP 200, Content-Type application/pdf, with 902859 bytes read in memory. All four web addresses printed in the markdown were checked with urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1: https://www.nber.org returned HTTP 200 (a cited institution homepage); https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18238 returned HTTP 200 (Ju and Aral, a different paper); https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.05196 returned HTTP 200 (Padmakumar and He, a different paper); https://www.unibocconishop.it returned HTTP 200 and redirected to https://www.unibocconishop.it/en_GB (the merchandise shop in the case stimulus). None identifies a deposit for c191.

No relevant data/code deposit was found in the requested DataCite, Zenodo, Harvard Dataverse and OSF searches, so there was no study deposit whose files or participant-level columns could be inspected. The broad surname searches included unrelated Figshare, Zenodo and OSF records; these were not misclassified as deposits for this paper. No GitHub repository is named, and no GitHub API quota was used.

For form study S1, no newly located public dataset permits the missing arm-level outcome means, SDs, SEs or analyzed counts, the Causal&GPT-versus-Causal contrasts with their SEs/tests, assignment-class clustered precision, or within-arm between-person semantic diversity to be computed. Scores plus arm indicators are needed for arm summaries; the adjusted contrasts and clustered precision also need model covariates and class identifiers or fitted-model covariances; diversity needs participant-linked texts, ideas or embeddings and an explicit weighting implementation. Accordingly what_we_could_compute is null.

Confidence is medium: the complete source and all four repository services were checked successfully, but CEPR returned HTTP 403 with a bot check, its possible supplementary files could not be inspected, the registration is unidentified, and repository searches cannot exclude an unindexed or differently titled deposit. No account was used, access requested, or access restriction bypassed.
